Pros and cons of the country you live in now.

I am originally from Southern California in the United States of America but in 1993 found myself living in the Capitol of the Czech Republic. It was quite difficult to understand the different ways that Czechs did things back then, for example you had to have a shopping cart or a basket if you went into a store. It literally took me a decade to figure out why this was but I finally realized that under the communist system the goal was to limit access to goods and services to the population. Hence, they had a limited number of baskets/carts in the store and everyone else had to wait outside until one became available. From what I heard, the lines were long. Flash forward to 2015 and this city has really come along. Instead of having to buy stuff by 18:00 (22:00 if you were lucky to live near a Vecerka (evening store)) now you can find shops, bars and restaurants who are more than happy to take your money at any time of the day. The Czech people seem very standoffish at first but if you look at their history (and the number of times they have been invaded by foreign powers (they have four National Holidays devoted to Independence for fucks sake)) you can fully understand why. Over the many years that I have made my own minor contributions to this amazing city I have seen the Czech people start to throw off their bunker mentality and really let their hair down. The Czech people can be a LOT of fun after you get a few beers in them. I do go back to SoCal occasionally and it always looks pretty much the same... Mc.D's...Safeway...Starbucks...Taco Bell...Walmart...Del Taco...Target...Burger King... rinse and repeat. You know what I am saying. Over here the small players still have a chance and some of the spaces that are created are sometimes strange but wholly original. I like the fact that living here I never have to worry about walking around at night by myself, I like the fact that (unless I pay attention) I don't have to listen to peoples banal conversations on public transport, I like the fact that when I go to the Doctors office I just show then my card (and give them a buck and a quarter, ouch), I like the fact that my children, when they grow up. will have free access to a University education, and I like the fact that I met the most awesome woman on the planet here in this city. I don't know what else to say, I can say that I miss the beach but I can also say that I don't miss earthquakes.

I'm from the Czech republic and I definitely agree with you. I'm 18 so I didn't live through the wild 90's so I can't say how far this country has come from my own experience but I definitely believe it's a much better place today. Prague is a very solid choice if you want to live fairly cheap in Europe.

The second post about the Czech Republic here so I will keep it short. I am writing this from the perspective of living in Prague but it should generally apply to the other parts too.

Pros:

Very low unemployment

Cheap

Lots of things to do

Amazing transportation system (Prague)

Best beer in the world (sorry Germans) that is incredibly cheap

Weed is easy to find and if the cops catch you all you get is a fine (unless you have more than 10g iirc).

Tons of historical buildings everywhere

Safe

Cons:

Wages can be quite low, but it depends where you work

Inefficient bureaucracy (but then again that is true for most countries)

The typical czech cuisine in my opinion isn't very good, luckily there are tons of restaurants with food from all over the world
